'''Soegawa Shrine''' (そえがわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located near the summit of {{ill|Mount Takaoka|Q17225894|qid=Q17225894|lt=Mount Takaoka}} in {{ill|Hachirōgata, Akita|arz|هاتشيروجاتا|ceb|Hachirōgata-machi|es|Hachirōgata (Akita)|fa|هاچیروگاتا، آکیتا|fi|Hachirōgata|fr|Hachirōgata (Akita)|id|Hachirōgata, Akita|it|Hachirōgata|ja|八郎潟町|ko|하치로가타정|ms|Hachirōgata, Akita|my|ဟချိရေားဂတမြို့၊ အခိတ|pl|Hachirōgata|ru|Хатирогата|tl|Hachirōgata, Akita|tr|Hachirōgata (kasaba)|uk|Хатіроґата (Акіта)|ur|ہاچیرؤگاتا، اکیتا|uz|Hachirōgata (Akita)|vi|Hachirōgata, Akita|zh|八郎潟町|qid=Q1205526}}, {{ill|Minamiakita District, Akita|Q1155694|qid=Q1155694}}, {{ill|Akita Prefecture|Q81863|qid=Q81863}}. It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=small shrine in the Engishiki}} (disputed), and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranks}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, when {{ill|Satake Yoshitada|Q8514533|qid=Q8514533}}, lord of the {{ill|Kubota Domain|Q1067720|qid=Q1067720|lt=Akita Domain}}, carried out the restoration of ancient shrines within the domain, this site was identified as the location of the Shikinaisha “Yamamoto District, one-seat small Soegawa Shrine,” leading to its revival. Throughout the Edo period, as one of the three principal shrines of the Akita Domain, it held a shrine estate of 30 koku.

Originally, {{ill|Yamamoto District, Akita|Q1155896|qid=Q1155896}} referred to what is now {{ill|Senboku District, Akita|ceb|Semboku-gun|fr|District de Senboku (Akita)|id|Distrik Senboku, Akita|it|Distretto di Senboku (Akita)|ja|仙北郡|kk|Сембоку (уезд, Акита)|ko|센보쿠군 (아키타현)|pl|Powiat Senboku|ru|Сембоку (уезд, Акита)|uk|Повіт Сембоку (Акіта)|zh|仙北郡|qid=Q733727}}. Plates excavated from the {{ill|Hotta-no-saku|Q11497278|qid=Q11497278}} also bear the inscription “Yamamoto.” There is a theory that, in order to identify the Shikinaisha “Yamamoto District, one-seat small Soegawa Shrine” with the present Soegawa Shrine, an area formerly called “Hiyama District” was renamed “Yamamoto District.”

Originally, {{ill|Mount Takaoka|Q17225894|qid=Q17225894|lt=Mount Takaoka}} had a shrine called Kōmine Shrine, whose enshrined deity was {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993}}. According to records, when the Kubota Domain was asked by the Yoshida family of Kyoto in {{ill|1714|Q6878|qid=Q6878}} about the existence of Soegawa Shrine, the domain’s shrine magistrate, Mogi Tomonori, regarded Mount Takaoka as a sacred site and established Soegawa Shrine by jointly enshrining Kōmine Shrine. Local elders say, “This place is called Hatarazawa and also Horoha-yama; though one mountain, it has eight valleys.” The *Gun’yūki* records, “It may be the main sanctuary of Mount Horoha.” Soegawa is also read as “Soikawa.”<ref>*The Gods and Shrines of Akita*, by Hisaji Satō, Akita Shinshū Research Association, 1981</ref>

[[File:Takaokayama Zyoyatô.JPG|thumb|right|Mount Takaoka – Soegawa Shrine stone lantern]]
The stone lantern at the third torii gate on the mountainside (commonly called the middle torii) was a permanent lantern approximately 2.5 meters tall. In the past, it served as a lighthouse for boats traveling across Hachirōgata Lagoon.

In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5), it was designated a Gōsha.

=== Northernmost Shikinaisha ===
In terms of its present location, it is the northernmost Shikinaisha in Japan. However, according to shrine tradition based on the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}, the original site of Soegawa Shrine was the present {{ill|Dake Rokusho Shrine|Q11477429|qid=Q11477429}}. As this view is supported by {{ill|Kogakkan University|Q1797584|qid=Q1797584}} and many local historians, the shrine that should be considered the northernmost in its original location is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiga Riwake Shrine}} in {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|Q48326|qid=Q48326}}. The disputed shrines for the Shikinaisha “Yamamoto District, one-seat small Soegawa Shrine” include this shrine, the aforementioned Take Rokushō Shrine, its village shrine Hachiman Shrine, and Soikawa Shinmei Shrine (present-day Soikawa, {{ill|Akita (city)|Q17139|qid=Q17139}}, Akita Prefecture).

=== Chronology ===
〈〉 indicates related events
* Around {{ill|701|Q23496|qid=Q23496}} ({{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taihō}} 1): Founded upon a petition by {{ill|Fujiwara no Fuhito|Q177517|qid=Q177517}} and others<ref name="akitajiten"/>
* {{ill|871|Q24754|qid=Q24754}} ({{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 13): Granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade<ref name="akitajiten"/>
* {{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 7): 〈{{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|Q1071525|qid=Q1071525}} enters Akita〉
* {{ill|1714|Q6878|qid=Q6878}} ({{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shōtoku}} 4): According to shrine tradition, relocated to the present site and restored by {{ill|Satake Yoshitada|Q8514533|qid=Q8514533}}
* March {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 1): 〈{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinbutsu bunri edict}}〉
* May 14, {{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}} (Meiji 4): 〈Establishment of the {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}}〉
* {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5): Listed as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}
* {{ill|1899|Q7851|qid=Q7851}}–{{ill|1900|Q2034|qid=Q2034}} (Meiji 32–33): A villager surnamed Yoshida discovered numerous octagonal mirrors while digging lakebed mud with a hoe. One, a Zuika Sōhō mirror from the Heian period, was preserved at Soegawa Shrine<ref>Isoo Ōba, *Studies in Shinto Archaeology*, 1943, p. 398</ref>.
* {{ill|1910|Q2075|qid=Q2075}} (Meiji 43): Uraōmachi Shinmei Shrine jointly enshrined<ref name="akitajiten"/>
* {{ill|1911|Q2076|qid=Q2076}} (Meiji 44): Kodachibana Inari Shrine jointly enshrined<ref name="akitajiten"/>
